summary: Frontend test of sessionOpenedAtRef (take-attendance.tsx) and the optional timestamp in addAttendanceRecord (offlineSyncStore.ts). I used a temporary lecture for teacher180156 dated today (2026-11-10, course 698f0000d803b27aab0120af, 72 students), which I created and later deleted. RESULT: the fix works ONLY in the explicit offline branch (the else branch, reached when offlineMode=true, i.e. the screen was loaded through loadCachedData). There, after a deliberate 10s wait, the stored timestamp equals the screen-open time (ts minus open time = -0.19s, save time minus ts = 13.45s). PASS. The exact flow described in the request (screen opened ONLINE, network lost, wait, save) still records the SAVE time: ts minus open time = +12.94s, ts is about 1s after the save click. FAIL. The same happens when the screen is reopened offline but the axios GET cache serves /lectures/{id}/details (+13.91s, FAIL). In both cases the code goes to the catch() fallback ('تم حفظ الحضور محلياً (فشل الاتصال بالخادم)'), and that fallback's addAttendanceRecord loop does NOT pass timestamp. Regressions: immediate offline save works (dialog shows '72 سجل معلق', ts = open time). Online save works (POST /attendance/session returned 200, 'تم حفظ الحضور بنجاح', no offline_recorded_at in the payload, 0 pending). The stale-cache guard still works (title 'محاضرة ليست لليوم', 0 rows, for a cached lecture dated 2026-11-07). I also found a serious data-loss race in offlineSyncStore that existed before this change: only 1 of 72 offline records was kept in storage.

ui_bugs.issue: data-testid='save-attendance-btn' is set on a RN TouchableOpacity without testID, so it is not rendered on web. Selected by text instead. Add testID.

integration_issues.flow: Open online, then lose network or app goes to background, then save (the main scenario of this fix)
integration_issues.issue: The catch() fallback in saveAttendance (around line 545-556, 'فشل اتصال حقيقي - حفظ أوفلاين') calls addAttendanceRecord WITHOUT timestamp, so the save time is still stored. This is the most common real path. isOnline stays true (NetInfo on web did not flip after context.set_offline(true); on native it can also lag or be flaky), and offlineMode is false because the screen was loaded online. So the online POST is attempted, fails, and falls to the catch block. Measured: ts minus open time = 12.94s for a 10s wait. Sync would then send offline_recorded_at = save time and the record is rejected unfairly.

integration_issues.flow: Reopen the lecture screen while offline when an axios GET cache exists
integration_issues.issue: The api.ts response interceptor returns the cached GET /lectures/{id}/details ('OK (cached)') on a network error. fetchData then treats it as an online success: setOfflineMode(false), and the 'وضع أوفلاين' pill is not shown. Save goes to the online POST, which fails, then to the catch fallback without a timestamp, so the save time is stored again (+13.91s). The good else branch is only reached when the cache_/lectures/{id}/details key is missing.

integration_issues.flow: offlineSyncStore.addAttendanceRecord + syncPendingRecords race (DATA LOSS, existed before this change)
integration_issues.issue: When isOnline is true (even if wrong), the FIRST addAttendanceRecord call in the save loop starts syncPendingRecords() without awaiting it. That call snapshots pendingRecords (1 record). The loop then adds the other 71 records. When the sync request fails or finishes, it runs set({pendingRecords: cleanedRecords}) from the stale snapshot, which overwrites and drops the 71 records added in the meantime. Seen in every offline/fallback run: the alert said '72 سجل معلق', but offline_pending_records in storage held only 1 record. Console: 'بدء مزامنة 1 سجل' then 'نتيجة المزامنة: 0 نجاح، 1 فشل'.

action_items: HIGH: In take-attendance.tsx, catch() fallback loop (around line 545-556), pass timestamp: sessionOpenedAtRef.current?.lectureId === lectureId ? sessionOpenedAtRef.current.ts : undefined to addAttendanceRecord, the same as the else branch. Better: put both loops in one helper so they cannot drift apart again.

HIGH: Fix the race in offlineSyncStore. In syncPendingRecords, merge the sync result into get().pendingRecords at the end (update only the records that were synced or failed, by local_id) instead of overwriting with the snapshot taken at the start. Or do not start a sync from inside addAttendanceRecord while the save loop is running (add a skipSync flag and sync once after the loop).
MEDIUM: Treat a response with statusText 'OK (cached)' from lecturesAPI.getDetails in fetchData as offline: setOfflineMode(true) and show the offline pill, so the correct offline branch is used.
LOW: Add testID='save-attendance-btn' to the save TouchableOpacity.
critical_code_review_comments: take-attendance.tsx is over 1000 lines. The offline save loop is duplicated in the else branch and in the catch fallback (DRY). This duplication is exactly why the timestamp fix was applied to only one of them.

Timing design: the open time is captured on the first successful data load per lectureId. A teacher who opens the screen hours BEFORE the lecture window and saves later would get an early timestamp. The backend grace check may then reject the record as 'not started yet'. Consider clamping, or recording the time of the first student toggle.
When an existing pending record is updated, its timestamp is overwritten with newRecord.timestamp. That is acceptable now, but it falls back to the save time whenever timestamp is undefined.

success_rate.frontend: 60% (3 of 5 scenarios passed: offline else-branch delayed save, offline immediate save, online save, stale guard; failed: the online-open then lost-network delayed save and the cached-details reopen both store the save time; plus the data-loss race)

context_for_next_testing_agent: To reproduce: create a lecture today for course 698f0000d803b27aab0120af with start_time about now in Aden time (UTC+3). The window closes 30 min after start. Scenario A: open /take-attendance?lectureId=X online, then context.set_offline(True), wait 10s, click the first student-row, click the text 'حفظ الحضور', then confirm-lesson-save. The alert shows the fallback message. Then route **/api/** abort, set_offline(False), go to '/' and read localStorage offline_pending_records[].timestamp. Scenario B (true offline branch): after one online load, remove localStorage keys cache_*<lectureId>*, abort **/api/**, then goto the lecture page. The 'وضع أوفلاين' pill shows, and the alert shows 'N سجل معلق'. Delete the test lecture and its attendance afterwards.
rca of the issue: The fix was applied only to the else branch (offlineMode || !isOnline). On web, and often on native, the real 'opened online, then lost connection' flow goes through the online POST. That POST fails with a network error and lands in the catch() fallback, which still calls addAttendanceRecord without a timestamp, so the store falls back to new Date() (the save time). The axios GET cache also hides offline loads as online loads (offlineMode=false). Separately, syncPendingRecords overwrites pendingRecords with a stale snapshot, which loses records added while a sync is in flight.
